statement: Every compact real-fiber interval between two actual prefix images at exactly the same lifted target level is contained in the compact three-word image f_u f_v^{-1} f_a(x), with 0 <= a <= v <= u <= 1. The exact containment holds first in the original universal source cover and then after its specified projection. It also holds for the inverse path. Across arbitrary varying open orbits and quotients, all such intervals remain compact and every accumulation point lies in the same original G-orbit as the limiting input point. At a fixed frontier point the entire interval shrinks to that point.
depends_on: C43 exact product chart for connected proper real fibers; C44 original source and target covering maps and deck labels; the based source lifts and their increasing real target maps; elementary winding in a punctured plane and compactness of actual global word parameters
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and full prefix-fiber interval control
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The opposite-side paths use the actual induced increasing target maps. Their disk is the explicit three-letter source word triangle, and every projection uses the original source cover and the same deck labels. The proof makes no assumption about an extended frontier foliation, quotient compactness, or bounded source coordinates.
notes: For each complementary excursion of the real base path away from its endpoint level, h_r A and g h_r^{-1} A lie on opposite sides of the original proper fiber. Their joined loop has winding plus or minus one around every interior point of its endpoint fiber interval. It bounds the actual triangle h_u h_v^{-1} A = f_u f_v^{-1} f_a(x), so the whole interval lies in the triangle image. Linear interpolation on the complementary gaps of the compact zero set proves that these excursion intervals and the zero-level track cover the original interval. The one compact global three-word family then gives uniform frontier control across all source orbits and covers. This excludes the remote nonopen limits and ambient escape left by C61 and proves complete interval shrinking at fixed frontier points. At a nonfixed limit orbit the compact word image can still contain several points; selection of the prescribed boundary value and a continuously varying lift of the nontrivial quotient deformation remain unresolved in C12.
